note: The book's style plate: every later picture uses it as the style reference.
style: A seventeenth-century French narrative oil painting in the manner of Meissonier and Maurice Leloir: academic realism, exact costume of 1625 (doublets, falling lace collars, wide-brimmed plumed felt hats, bucket-top boots, rapiers and baldrics), warm candlelight and golden daylight against blue Paris dusk, rich glazes, fine brushwork. One single painting filling the whole frame edge to edge; no text, lettering, signature, monogram, border or black bars.

beats.text: The courtyard of a coaching inn in the town of Meung on the Loire in April 1625, golden afternoon light: a timber-framed inn with a painted sign of a jolly miller, townsfolk gathered, a young Gascon cavalier on a strange yellow pony at the gate, a gentleman in a violet doublet watching from a ground-floor window, horses, a well, blue sky with spring clouds. A wide establishing view.
